item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
You get a downvote, and you get a downvote, and YOU get a downvote!
I really don't feel like this is a very helpful article to anyone. Unlike some other places, a downvote here is not just telling the world 'I didn't like it', rather 'This should not even exist'.
To get meta, that's why I'm -1ing this article. I fundamentally disagree with the notion that voting is anything to joke about, and thus jokes about it shouldn't exist.

And it is a joke. Much of it past raw grammar is extremely subjective. And while readers are entitled to downvote simply cause they didn't like an article for reason X, I personally try hard to avoid doing so. I don't think simple dislike should equate a downvote; I hope any future members do not fall into the cognitive pit trap this article papers over with cheeky humor.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
682 is dangerous and, over the years, has become increasingly interesting.

There is nothing stopping a dangerous Keter from showing up and advancing to high numbers quickly. But being dangerous isn't sufficient. I could easily say SCP-3000 is a Keter uncontainable monster that kills everything at a rate of billions every second, but will it last? No.

SCP-2845 requires extensive containment because of the value of ritual.
SCP-2317 is a discussion on the depths the Foundation will lie to itself for peace of mind.
SCP-2006 reminds us all what fear is, philosophically.
SCP-2950 demonstrates how perception is reality.
SCP-2460 pushes hard science to the limit with a plausible interpretation that's terrifying.

Danger doesn't drive the value of each SCP. It serves as a tool for telling the story that lies beneath the danger.

And SCP-682 is a story on the challenges and resources we go through to contain something that is ultimately unstoppable.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I do believe the bad shoppery, or using a clearly hand-drawn/badly-CGI'd image and claiming it to be the "actual" thing, or an "artist's rendering" of the actual thing, is plain ridiculous. The only time I let that fly is if A) the thing causes some sort of visual distortion that MAKES it look that way, B) the "actual thing" is some sort of image (painting, .JPG file, whatever) or C) it's a representation of a shape/object that isn't directly observable (invisible, visual distortions, etc) but absolutely MUST be shown for whatever. Also note that C is very, very rarely used effectively.
